text:
Maya (Support): Heads up — customer acme-corp reporting hourly usage in Console is ~3 hours behind (hourly rollups). Started around 2026-03-17 06:30 UTC. Ticket SUP-1247, link: https://console.redwood.ai/acme/usage :eyes:

Benji (SRE): thx, any errors in pipeline logs? did anything change (kafka, consumers, deploy) around 06:30? :thinking_face:

Maya (Support): Customer noticed after we rotated brokers at 06:40. They saw spikes then gap. No deploys on infra. Ingest-bot showed consumer group rebalance events at 06:41.

Carla (DataEng): @Benji can you check consumer offsets for group `usage-rollup-v2`? run:```bash
kafka-consumer-groups.sh --describe --group usage-rollup-v2 --bootstrap-server kafka-1:9092
```I suspect partition shift left some offsets uncommitted.

Benji (SRE): running now, giving results...

ingest-bot: consumer_group:usage-rollup-v2 rebalance detected, members: 4 -> 3, reason: broker-restart

Benji (SRE): output shows some partitions at older offsets, one partition (topic=events-tenant-42-part-3) lag is huge (~1.2M messages). consumer lag spiked during rebalance. Looks like one pod failed to commit.

Dmitri (Backend): Could be that the rollup worker crashed while processing long event window and didn't checkpoint. Any crash traces?

Benji (SRE): found stack trace from pod rollup-processor-2: `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` at 06:40:23. Pod restarted and rejoined, left unprocessed backlog.

Carla (DataEng): OK that explains backlog. We should kick a targeted backfill for the affected tenant partitions rather than whole-day backfill. I'll run ad-hoc rollup backfill for tenant `acme-corp` for the missing window. Command I will use:
```bash
kubectl -n data run --rm -i backfill --image=redwood/rollup-tools:prod -- 
  backfill-rollups --tenant acme-corp --start 2026-03-17T03:00Z --end 2026-03-17T10:00Z --partitions 3
```

Maya (Support): please note customer expects hourly chart continuity. I'll message them that we have the backfill scheduled and will confirm when Console reflects it.

Benji (SRE): also throttling is happening on the consumer due to GC pauses; increasing memory on rollup pods to 12Gi and bumping JVM flags to `-XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200` to avoid restart loop. Deploying now. :hammer_and_wrench:

ingest-bot: backfill job queued (job_id: bf-20260317-01), status: queued

Carla (DataEng): kicked job bf-20260317-01, monitoring progress. If it stalls we can run partition-specific consumer replay using `kafka-console-consumer` and the rollup lambda locally.

Benji (SRE): I've scaled rollup deployment to 4 replicas and applied memory bump. Rolling restart done at 07:05 UTC. No further OOMs in last 20m.

ingest-bot: backfill job bf-20260317-01 status: running (processed 12%)

Maya (Support): told customer: "We're running a targeted backfill and increased worker memory. Expect charts to catch up within 2-4 hours; I'll update as soon as Console shows corrections." :thumbsup:

Carla (DataEng): backfill at 90% now, should finish in ~8 minutes. After completion I'll trigger quick reconcile job to regenerate hourly rollups index.

ingest-bot: backfill job bf-20260317-01 status: succeeded, duration: 00:28:12

Carla (DataEng): done. reconcile kicked: `reconcile-hourly-rollups --tenant acme-corp --check-only=false`

Benji (SRE): Console ingestion pipeline acked new rollups. Visible in staging console. Pushing to prod indexer now.

Maya (Support): Customer confirmed charts updated and gaps filled at 09:05 UTC. Closing ticket if no regressions. Thanks all. :tada:

Dmitri (Backend): follow-up action: add watchdog to detect long consumer GC/OOM cycles and auto-scale before restart. Filed ENG-1983.

Carla (DataEng): add a backfill playbook section for targeted partition replays so support can triage faster. Filed DOCS-412.

Maya (Support): marking resolved in SUP-1247. Closing thread.
